knowledge_point.title: Finding the Equation of a Line Perpendicular to a Line Through Two Points

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(-5,-6)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(-1,2)$ and $(-6,8).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes which are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(-1,2)$ and $(-6,8):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{-6-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{6}{-5} \\  & =- \frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (- \frac{6}{5})=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{5}{6}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(-5,-6).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-6) & =\frac{5}{6}(x-(-5)) \\ y+6 & =\frac{5}{6}(x+5) \\ y+6 & =\frac{5 x}{6} + \frac{25}{6} \\ y & =\frac{5 x}{6} - \frac{11}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the point $(-2,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line passing through the points $(6,1)$ and $(4,5).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Perpendicular lines have slopes which are negative reciprocals of each other.

First, let's find the slope ${m}_{1}$ of the line passing through the points $(6,1)$ and $(4,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{5-1}{4-6} \\  & =\frac{4}{-2} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want a perpendicular line, the slope $m$ of the line we're trying to find must satisfy

$$
m\cdot (-2)=-1\,⇒\,m=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

We know that the line passes through the point $(-2,5).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-(-2)) \\ y-5 & =\frac{1}{2}(x+2) \\ y-5 & =\frac{1}{2}x+1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}x+6\end{aligned}
$$
